summary: Compute the Moore-Penrose inverse of a finite real matrix, discarding singular values below a relative threshold.

identity.definition: For M = U diag(s) V^T, return V diag(1/s for s >= rcond else 0) U^T.
identity.model: truncated singular-value decomposition of a dense real matrix
identity.geometry: dense real matrix without spatial geometry
identity.coordinates: dimensionless matrix entries; rcond is a relative scalar threshold
identity.boundary: singular values below rcond are discarded; non-2-D, non-finite or non-positive-threshold inputs are rejected
assumptions: The input is a finite real matrix.
rcond is a positive finite relative threshold.
NumPy singular-value ordering and sign conventions are used.

inputs.name: mat
inputs.description: finite real matrix whose pseudo-inverse is requested

supported: rank-deficient spectra with thresholded singular values
excluded: iterative or regularized least-squares semantics beyond truncation

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised for non-2-D or non-finite matrices and for a non-positive or non-finite rcond.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: No additional runtime failure is defined; NumPy floating-point behavior applies.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the computation is a direct decomposition.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No partial result is returned after invalid input.

example.description: Invert a rank-deficient two-by-two matrix and a rectangular matrix.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.geometry import truncated_svd_inverse
m = np.array([[1., 2.], [2., 4.]])
assert np.allclose(truncated_svd_inverse(m), np.linalg.pinv(m))
r = truncated_svd_inverse(np.ones((5, 3)))
assert r.shape == (3, 5)
example.expected: The truncated inverse equals the NumPy pseudo-inverse on the rank-deficient case and preserves the (n,m) shape.

scope: Agreement with numpy.linalg.pinv on square, tall and wide full-rank matrices.
Rank-deficient thresholding and the M M^+ M = M projection identity.
Rejection of non-2-D and non-finite matrices and of non-positive or non-finite thresholds.
verification.evidence_ceiling: Mathematical identity checks on bounded dense matrices; no application-level diagnostic-fitting or statistical-error claim.
known_limitations: Complex and sparse matrices are not supported.
rcond follows NumPy singular-value conventions; it is not a statistical noise model.
No iterative, weighted or regularized least-squares semantics are provided.
